turns.t: Morning. Spring's started and my eyes are streaming, itching, the lot. I want my usual sorted before it gets bad, so can we go through it quickly?
Of course. Tell me what you're using at the moment.
Olopatadine eye drops, twice a day. Cetirizine, 10 mg, once a day. Fluticasone nasal spray, two sprays once a day. And montelukast, 10 mg, maybe? At night? I take it for the asthma.
And is the montelukast 10 mg? You said maybe.
It's 10, I'm fairly sure. It might be 5. I'd have to check the box.
I'll check the record, that's fine. Which of those is working best? ~
The cetirizine, and the eye drops. The nasal spray I use when I remember. ~
How have your eyes been this week? ~
Itchy and watery, but not red. I can cope. I'd just like to be ahead of it. ~
Sensible. And your wider health, what do you have on the record?
Hay fever, obviously, asthma, since I was a child, and eczema. Classic trio.
Any operations?
A squint operation, when I was four.
Thank you. How's your asthma at the moment? ~
Quiet. Spring and summer tend to be when it kicks in, but it's fine now. ~
Good. Here's what I suggest, given the season. Start the nasal spray now, every day, rather than occasionally, because it works by building up.
Right. I've been inconsistent. ~
And start the cetirizine and the eye drops a week before your worst weeks, if you can predict them.
Mid-May usually. ~
Then start in early May. Keep windows closed in the morning, shower when you get in, and wipe your eyes with a cool damp cloth.
I do all that, mostly. ~
Wear wraparound sunglasses, it keeps pollen off your eyes. ~
I've got some, in the car. ~
I'd like to see you again in six weeks, to see how the season's going and check your asthma.
Six weeks. Right, thank you. ~
You're welcome. Do you want the reminder in writing? ~
Yes, please, on the prescription slip. ~
I'll print it with the repeat prescriptions. ~
Marvellous. Same drugs, nothing new? ~
Nothing new, just using them in a smarter order. ~

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient gave the montelukast dose tentatively ("10 mg, maybe? ... it might be 5").

clinical_actions.description: Use the nasal spray daily to build up effect
Start cetirizine and eye drops a week before the worst weeks
Close bedroom windows in the morning, shower on getting in, use cool damp cloths and wraparound sunglasses
